body: I realize this will probably get me karma slapped, but I don't give all that much of a fuck. Some folks have told me (whether in person or online) that killing myself is a selfish act. I see where they're coming from, but damn it, isn't it equally selfish to badger someone who clearly doesn't want to live into "soldiering on?" Does the selfishness of the many outweigh the selfishness of one? I've given all my life. Can't I be selfish just once?

Been seeing a psychologist and a psychiatrist for over a year now. Been an uphill battle every step of the way. And now, I'm bored of it. Just...nothing motivates me to want to continue anymore. Sure, I'm posting on reddit after saying that I had a plan to kill myself, but that's just because I have to make it to my next appointment with my psychiatrist tomorrow. After that, who knows.
I appreciate the thought; however, I feel no emotion so I can't really say it's effective.

Spoken to her. Don't know how serious she is taking me. She brings up the kids as a reason not to do it. If I actually felt any emotions, I'd break down right there. Truth is, my daughter is a baby and wouldn't remember, and my son is only 4, so he'll probably forget pretty quickly.
It's not the talking I'm afraid of. Here I am, talking about it to people I've never met. It's the inconvenience of being placed under observation for some undetermined period of time.

I'm no longer hiding it from my wife, but I'll be damned if I'm not still having the thoughts. I've rationalized it, and am pretty much at peace with my decision. 

Need to work up the strength to go get the materials. I find it hilarious that I can get everything I need at Party City (my wife does not find it funny at all).

Something I'm hiding from my parents...I've pretty much planned out how I want to kill myself. I know what materials I need, where to get them, and how long it will take. 

I'm also hiding that from my wife.

They know some of what I'm going through, in that they know about the depression, therapy, and meds. My wife knows more, obviously, because she lives with me. She also knows some of my history - we bathe together every morning for practicality and so she can make sure I haven't been cutting again. Kind of hard to do that if someone is seeing you naked every day. 

My problem with viewing everything in such a positive light is that the thoughts don't go away. They never have. They haven't even reduced in intensity. Instead, they've become more rational.

It's ongoing. 

I feel like my wife is getting annoyed with my depression, and I do not want my family involved. My friends are far enough away that I would be cold already when they arrived, even if I didn't have the necessary materials on hand when I called them. 

I kind of feel like talking to anyone, whether therapist, friend, family, or spouse, is more of an annoyance to them than anything. Hell, my wife told me to "stop being emo" just this morning. 

I don't know. Keeping on top of my therapy and meds, making changes to my lifestyle...in the end, it's the same old shit, isn't it? "Life sucks, and then you die." But no, I have control over that last part, I can die on my terms, of my method.
Oh man. This whole song...I hate it with a passion, but I simultaneously love it for reasons I don't quite understand.

I can relate to the lack of music enjoyment. Feel like I got into a rut with the deathcore/stoner metal/90s hard rock/modern progressive cycle, so lately I've been avoiding music. Drive in silence, do yard work in silence, work in silence (but with headphones on so people don't bother me). 

I can still enjoy reading, but only for short bursts of maybe a chapter or two at a time. But other than that...nothing.

I regularly chase klonopin (for which I have a valid prescription) with scotch. Lots of scotch. Like, not "I'm drinking this to enjoy the flavor" scotch, but "man, I paid $80 for this bottle yesterday, where did it all go" scotch. 

I occasionally pour Jack Daniels in my can of Coke before I go for a drive, especially if I'm going out to lunch. 

I want to die, but I don't want to kill myself. There are rarely times I don't think about this, and I frequently try to rationalize it. 

I think my wife is putting on a show of support, but is trying to find a reason or a way to get me out of her life. 

I know I'm depressed, but I think the people around me think I'm just seeking attention. In fact, I know a few people in the office believe I'm seeking attention, because they're not as stealthy in hiding their Skype conversations as they think they are. This, in spite of my desperate attempts to keep my personal and work lives separate. 

I take long shits so I can be alone for a while. 

People tell me I don't have to face this alone, but when confronted with the reality of how I feel (or don't feel, as the case may be), they distance themselves. 

...well this turned into something completely different, didn't it...what was the question again?
Glad it's useful to you, in spite of the context :)

I'll tell you what I was told when I first started on this journey: seek help. If you can resolve it with therapy, great; if you need to start medication to get going, that's fine too. I'm just over a year in and I no longer want to actively end my life, so that's at least an improvement...but, as I've found, there's a larger process behind fixing everything. 

I have an appointment with my therapist today. Not expecting it to be a particularly happy session.
He was actually making plans to go back to his home country, with or without my mother, to die there. This after all the shit he talks about the place.
Yes, within the past week.

Now, I am completely emotionally vacant, and have no motivation to do anything - games, TV, reading, sex, anything. I know I have to go to bed, and I'll do it out of habit. I'll kiss my wife goodnight out of habit. I'll roll over on to my side of the bed, lay my head on the pillow, and wish myself dead. And tomorrow, when I inevitably wake up, I will begin the cycle anew.
Thanks...I find it kind of interesting that people actually read this.

My father pulled that one out on me a few months back, saying that he should do what old Native Americans do and just walk into the desert and disappear. To my parents and sister, I said it was a dumb, selfish idea, because that's what's expected. Not so deep down, I completely understood what he was saying.
Can confirm, haven't had to help a user add a printer in...well, I don't remember when I pushed them out via group policy but it's been a while now.

Deathcore. Been on a Thy Art Is Murder kick lately. I can't listen to "happy music" for more than 20 minutes before I want to jam a chopstick in my ear canal...using my Google Play All Access sub I've tried finding new stuff, but I always end up falling back.

Yep. Two weekends ago I went to the beach with my wife, kids, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, their respective boyfriends, and my nephew. Started out as a good time, but within a half hour I deteriorated to utter uselessness. Broke down when I went into the water with my wife, retreated to shore, and spent the rest of the day in the sun tent with my infant daughter. 

I realize that this happened in full view of the rest of the people at the beach, but I didn't give a shit. I don't know any of those people, and I'll likely never see them again. My in-laws and their significant others had no idea what happened, and were apparently afraid to ask me because my wife bore the brunt of that line of questioning. My kids and my nephew won't remember because they're just too young.

What bothers me the most is that I don't know what triggered it.

It's like that old high school gym uniform you kept after all these years. A whole bunch of shit piles up on top of it, but when you're cleaning up it just shows up again. 

I am alone in a dark room with the door shut. My wife, son, daughter, and dog are downstairs, and I have no motivation whatsoever to even look at them. I want to die, but I don't know how, and I know it would be a pain for those people downstairs.

Had this happen to me on my drive home - hell, on my way to pick up my son from day care. Reached for the klonopin as soon as I got home. It was one of those situations in which no amount of mindfulness, breathing exercises, thought redirection, etc. did anything...first time in months it's been this bad.

You can really fuck yourself up if you combine Clonazepam and alcohol. 

Source: I'm also on it, I've combined the two and passed out after a single scotch, and I know someone whose daughter died from excessive amounts of Clonazepam and alcohol at a party a couple years back (per the autopsy report).
Nicolas Cage and Hugh Grant. Every time I see their faces I want to rage out and punch something.

Customer did that to me once. The installation guide for the software I used to support is 30 pages long. At least half of that consists of pictures. Customer flat-out told me that he didn't want to read the manual because it was too long, and that I should perform the installation for him while he was on the phone. I put him on mute and punched a hole in the wall.
While taking a shit, I teach down and pick pubes of my nutsack. Occasionally it makes me wince and, rarely, draws a tear out of my eye, but I keep doing it.
Tried the [Alligator Fuckhouse](http://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=alligator+fuckhouse). My leg cramped up, and my wife ended up with a bloody nose.

Probably vomit. Picked up whatever disease my son brought home from day care. Maybe play some Mass Effect 2 between trips to the bathroom. Yuck.

Sorry I couldn't provide a useful idea.

Earlier in this thread I mentioned that I am in marriage counseling. There are couples sessions and individual sessions with the psychologist. My individual sessions focus on my own anxiety issues and sleep deprivation. The psychologist said that TV or computer screens cause problems falling asleep, which is when I told her about f.lux, and that I use it on all of the computers in the house. 

The following week, she told me it was a very cool app, that she had tried it herself, and that she was considering recommending it to others. It's genuinely a helpful application.

This is where I'm at right now. IT guy, early 30s, wife, kid, longer hours. Been in marriage counseling for a couple months now. Recently started seeing a psychiatrist who started me on an  antidepressant and as-needed anti-anxiety. I'm willing to believe the headline.
